question: Does quantile-mapping ERA5 onto IMD's gauge-based distribution fix the 'the model has never seen a cloudburst' problem?
method: Monotone piecewise-linear CDF match from ERA5 daily monsoon totals to IMD gridded daily totals, fitted on TRAIN YEARS ONLY (<=2023) over the wide NW-India domain (2,793 IMD cells x 7 monsoons). Applied to hourly values by correcting each DAY's total and distributing the correction across that day's hours in proportion to ERA5's own hourly shape.
why_that_hourly_assumption_is_defensible: We measured that ERA5 gets the TIMING right and the MAGNITUDE wrong: its 28 Jun 2024 peak landed at 22:00Z 27 Jun = 03:30 IST, matching the reported cloudburst hour, while its magnitude was off ~7x. So preserving the hourly shape and rescaling the daily total follows our own evidence.

skill_at_the_charter_threshold.head: 15 mm/h within 3 h, on the MAPPED target
skill_at_the_charter_threshold.vs_shipped_p5_head: shipped p5_w3 has higher ABSOLUTE CSI (0.121) but at an ERA5-scale 5 mm threshold; the mapped 15 mm head has better RELATIVE skill (2.8x persistence and 84x raw GFS, against 2.5x and 8x) at a threshold that means what it says

honest_limits: The mapped target is a statistically transformed ERA5, NOT a gauge measurement. We predict 'ERA5 rescaled onto the IMD distribution' — closer to reality than raw ERA5, but not ground truth.
IMD gridded is 0.25 deg and gauge-INTERPOLATED. We do not have IMD station data; it is not free and our accounts are unapproved. Say that rather than implying we do.
Quantile mapping matches DISTRIBUTIONS, not individual events. It cannot make the model detect a storm ERA5 missed entirely — only put the ones it did see on the right scale.
Fitted on train years only, so no test-year rainfall enters the target.
recommendation: ADOPT. It restores the charter's own 15 mm/h head from 63 test positives to 3,235, makes the thresholds match IMD's published categories, and improves relative skill against both baselines. Requires retraining all RainCast heads and updating the deck.
